journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The Tab key press event on the departure date input is being prevented (defaultPrevented: true), blocking focus movement to the next field. This occurs because the datepicker component does not handle the Tab key to allow default focus traversal when the calendar is open.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a Tab keydown listener to the datepicker input that hides the calendar without preventing the Tab key's default action. This ensures focus moves to the next field while closing the datepicker popup.

constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
    super(element, config)

    this._calendar = null
    this._isShown = false
    this._onTabKeyDown = null

    this._initCalendar()
  }

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation will move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected, allowing keyboard users to traverse the form sequentially. The datepicker popup will close when tabbing out, maintaining a predictable interface.
functional_risks: The Tab keydown listener might conflict with other keyboard handlers if they exist, though none are present in the current codebase.
Hiding the calendar on Tab key press could interfere with explicit Tab key usage within the calendar (if supported), but the calendar does not currently support Tab navigation internally.
Adding event listeners increases memory usage slightly, but the impact is negligible as listeners are properly disposed.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the datepicker calendar closes when tabbing out of the departure date field.
Verify that pressing Tab still works when the datepicker is not open (e.g., after selecting a date).
Verify that Shift+Tab (reverse tabbing) still functions correctly for other fields.
Verify that date selection via mouse or keyboard within the calendar continues to work as expected.

plan.root_cause: The Tab keydown event on the datepicker input has defaultPrevented set to true, likely due to a vanilla-calendar-pro (VCP) keydown listener that calls preventDefault() on Tab key. This blocks the browser's default focus navigation to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the datepicker input that calls stopImmediatePropagation() on Tab key to prevent VCP's listener from running, then hides the calendar. This allows the browser's default focus move to proceed while closing the datepicker popup.

class Datepicker extends BaseComponent {
  protected declare _element: HTMLElement & { value: string }
  protected declare _config: DatepickerConfig
  protected declare _calendar: Calendar | null
  protected declare _isShown: boolean
  protected declare _isInput: boolean
  protected declare _isInline: boolean
  protected declare _boundInput: HTMLInputElement | null
  protected declare _positionElement: HTMLElement
  protected declare _displayElement: HTMLElement | false | null
  protected declare _themeObserver: MutationObserver | null
  protected declare _themeAncestor: Element | null | undefined
  protected declare _onOutside: (event: Event) => void
  protected declare _onTriggerClick: () => void
  protected declare _onTabKeyDownCapture: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void | null

constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
    super(element, config)

    this._calendar = null
    this._isShown = false
    this._onTabKeyDownCapture = null

    this._initCalendar()
  }

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field as expected. The datepicker popup closes when tabbing out, maintaining a predictable keyboard interface.
functional_risks: Capture-phase listener might interfere with other capture-phase listeners (unlikely in this codebase).
stopImmediatePropagation prevents all other keydown listeners on the input for Tab key, but the calendar doesn't use Tab internally.
Direct addEventListener usage bypasses EventHandler, but is necessary for capture phase.
verification_requirements: Verify Tab from departure date moves focus to passengers field.
Verify datepicker calendar closes when tabbing out.
Verify Tab works when datepicker not open.
Verify date selection via mouse/keyboard in calendar works.
